The whole of [Melody](elements-melody.qmd) on one sheet. Every ▶ plays the example. Press **Full screen** to put the sheet on the whole screen for
revision or for the class board.

## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Melody: describing a tune"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### Conjunct
<p>Moving by step, to the next note up or down. A <strong>narrow</strong> range.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
C D E F|E D C2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Disjunct
<p>Moving by leap, jumping over notes. A <strong>wide</strong> range.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
C c G, e|A, a E c'|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Sequence
<p>The same idea again, starting higher or lower. (<strong>Repetition</strong>: again, unchanged.)</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
CDEC D2 z2|DEFD E2 z2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Imitation
<p>One part copies an idea another part has just played, often at a different pitch.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
V:1
GABG c2 G2|ABcA d2 A2|]
V:2 clef=bass
z8|G,A,B,G, C2 G,2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Ostinato
<p>A short idea repeated over and over. In the bass: a <em>ground bass</em> or a <em>riff</em>.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="104" data-style="rock"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:Am
"Am"A,2 CE A2 GE|"F"A,2 CE A2 GE|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Scalic
<p>Runs up and down the scale.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
C D E F|G A B c|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Triadic
<p>Uses the notes of the chords (broken chords).</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"C"C E G c|"G"B G D G|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Chromatic
<p>Notes outside the key, often moving by [half step]{.nn}. (<strong>Pentatonic</strong>: only five notes.)</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
E ^D E ^F G ^G A ^A|B c ^c d ^d e2 z|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Intervals
<p>Count the letter names, <strong>both ends included</strong>: C to E is C-D-E, a 3rd. Here: 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="80"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
C D C E|C F C G|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Scale degrees
<p>1 tonic · 2 supertonic · 3 mediant · 4 subdominant · 5 dominant · 6 submediant · 7 leading note. The tonic is home; the leading note pulls up to it.</p>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="melody"></div>
:::::

::::::
:::::::

## Describing a melody

- Shape (rising, falling, an arch), movement (conjunct or disjunct), range (narrow or wide), then what it is made of
  (scalic, triadic, chromatic) and how ideas come back (repetition, sequence, imitation).
- Ornaments (trills, mordents, turns): [Grace Notes and Ornaments](grace-notes-ornaments.qmd).

- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 5: Melody](elements-melody.qmd).
